question: Will Rafael Leao stay at AC Milan?
rules:
This market will resolve to the next team Rafael Leao officially joins by September 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

If Rafael Leao does not officially join a new team by September 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "AC Milan".

If Rafael Leao joins a team that is not listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

If Rafael Leao is released, retires, or is not under contract with any professional team by September 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

An official transfer announcement prior to the market's close date will immediately resolve this market to the corresponding option.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official announcements from AC Milan and/or the acquiring team. A consensus of credible media reporting may also be used to resolve the market.

evidence.excerpt: AC Milan announced that Rafael Alexandre da Conceição Leão had renewed his contract with the club until 30 June 2028.

MilanNews reported that Leão was recovering from muscular fatigue and would gradually resume work during the coming week. Its August 16 training update separately identified Fofana, Nkunku, Tomori and Odogu as training apart with a dedicated coach while awaiting moves.

Following Milan's friendly against Manchester United, Ruben Amorim said Leão's injury did not appear serious, although his availability for the league opener was uncertain. He said Leão was a Milan player and that the club was happy with him, while leaving his transfer-market situation open. Amorim also said Leão would have to compete for his place with Cissè, Saelemaekers and the returning Pulisic.

MilanNews documented Leão's response to a social-media post relaying claims that Amorim regarded him as a negative influence in Milan's dressing room. Leão replied, "Maybe you’re because you lying," disputing the allegation.

La Gazzetta dello Sport reported that Amorim preferred Leão to be sold, although he was not among the four players formally excluded from the project. It reported that Milan's acceptable transfer fee had fallen from €50–60 million to approximately €40–45 million.

Football Italia reported that the offers received for Leão were from Beşiktaş, Galatasaray and Fenerbahçe, and that none approached Milan's €50 million plus €10 million asking price. Citing Sky Sport Italia, it said Leão was expected to meet Gerry Cardinale the following week because the anticipated offers had not materialised. The article suggested that a contract-extension discussion could follow.

ANSA reported that Leão had spent weeks telling the Portuguese press he wanted to leave Milan but now wanted to stay because the few clubs that had approached him, including Galatasaray, were not to his liking. The report followed a meeting between Gerry Cardinale and Ruben Amorim concerning Milan's squad and outgoing transfers.
